title: Rediscovering Rest
coreMove: Rest becomes real when it stops auditioning for future output; protect a few shared, prepared, atelic pauses that need no payoff beyond being lived.

exampleSpecs.audience: advocates tempted to defend leisure through output
exampleSpecs.stakes: A public anti-overwork argument may keep productivity as the final measure of rest.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the Take Back Your Time case being revised away from productivity logic.

exampleSpecs.audience: families and hosts who want rest to survive the meal
exampleSpecs.stakes: Private willpower will fail unless stopping is prepared and socially protected.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Judith Shulevitz's sabbath account as shared protection for stopping.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who turn every gathering into useful output
exampleSpecs.stakes: A study of sabbath may be absorbed into recruitment and growth metrics.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Walter Brueggemann's resistance frame before the group becomes another production engine.

exampleSpecs.audience: walkers who turn leisure into tracking, posting, or self-improvement
exampleSpecs.stakes: A walk can be converted into content or allowed to remain its own reward.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Let the Yorkshire Dales walk stand as value in the doing itself.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A workplace rest policy can become another performance tool if its value depends on later output.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Remove productivity as the sole justification for a rest practice.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who feel guilty when leisure has no visible result
exampleSpecs.stakes: Early discomfort can be mistaken for evidence that rest is wrong or wasteful.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use John Gray's warning to interpret the first unease of idleness.
